name: ES Aggressor Clock Compression v1
instrument: ES transaction-timing signal executed with one MES using recorded MBP-1 quotes
source: Databento GLBX.MDP3 ES trades and MES MBP-1
hypothesis: Aggressor sides are competing point processes. A side with more variable exchange-event interarrival times is arriving in compressed bursts rather than sustaining smooth participation. Near the pre-close boundary, that bursty side is more likely to represent deadline urgency that has already exhausted, so price should move against it into the close.

signal.side_interarrivals: successive ts_event differences within each aggressor side, in nanoseconds
signal.side_burstiness: population standard deviation of positive side interarrivals divided by their mean
signal.equal_or_insufficient_rule: no trade if burstiness is equal or either side has fewer than three positive interarrivals
signal.interpretation: fade the side whose aggression is more temporally clustered

eligibility.entry_and_exit_quotes: finite, positive, non-crossed recorded MBP-1 bid and ask
eligibility.spread_filter: none; cross the recorded spread regardless of width

execution.entry_time: first MES MBP-1 record at or after 15:30:05 ET
execution.stop: none; one MES and a fixed approximately 29-minute holding period bound exposure
execution.exit_time: first recorded MES MBP-1 quote at or after 15:59:45 ET
execution.position_limit: one MES and at most one trade per RTH session

economics.slippage_model: the full recorded MES bid-ask spread is crossed at entry and exit; no additional modeled slippage

lesson: Relative aggressor-side burstiness was not directional. Fading the more clustered point process lost in every year and both directions. Following it, changing timestamps, or substituting another burstiness statistic would be result-derived rescue and is prohibited.
holdout_policy: 2024-2025 was not evaluated because the unchanged rule failed its development gates.
prohibited_posthoc_changes: following rather than fading the burstier side
using receive timestamps, fixed time bins, counts, medians, maxima, or another burstiness statistic
combining timing with price, trade size, or net flow
changing either trade or quote window
weekday, volatility, volume, or regime filters
